headline: Cyber Security Salary in the UK 2026: Average Pay by Level, Role and City
metaDescription: Cyber security salary UK 2026: median pay near £55,000, junior to CISO ranges, London premium, contractor day rates and top certifications. Latest trends.

sections.content:
Cyber security professionals in the UK earn a median gross salary of about £55,000 in 2026, placing them well above the national median full-time wage of roughly £35,000. Most analysts fall between £38,000 at the 10th percentile and £90,000 at the 90th percentile, with financial services, government, and consulting firms paying at the top of the range.

Junior analysts with zero to two years of experience typically start between £28,000 and £40,000. Mid-level professionals with three to five years earn around £55,000, while seniors with six or more years average near £72,000. Demand remains strong: employers continue to report hiring difficulty, and salaries have kept rising faster than the broader tech market.
sections.title: 2026 Pay Benchmarks by Experience

sections.content:
London roles pay 25 to 35 percent above the national average, with a median near £69,800, reflecting the concentration of banks, consultancies, and tech firms. Bristol averages about £60,000 and Manchester around £58,000, while the South East and Thames Valley sit between London and the national figure. The rise of remote and hybrid working has softened but not erased the London premium.

By role, SOC analysts earn £25,000 to £75,000 depending on level, penetration testers £28,000 to £95,000, and security engineers £35,000 to £95,000. Security architects reach £85,000 to £120,000 at senior level, incident response specialists £70,000 to £100,000, and CISOs £120,000 to £250,000-plus. Contractors add a further premium: mid-level analysts charge £400 to £550 a day and cleared senior specialists exceed £900.
sections.title: Pay by Role, City and Contract Rate

sections.content:
Certifications carry unusual weight in cyber security. CompTIA Security+ opens analyst and SOC roles for entrants, while CISSP typically adds £10,000 to £20,000 to salary and is almost mandatory at director level. OSCP moves penetration testers into the £70,000 to £95,000 band, and cloud security credentials like AWS Security Specialty push engineers toward £120,000-plus.

The biggest pay jumps come from specialisation: cloud security, penetration testing, and incident response lift pay well above general analyst rates. Government and finance roles requiring SC or DV clearance pay premiums because the cleared talent pool is small. With demand projected to keep outpacing supply, candidates who combine a recognised certificate with hands-on cloud or defensive tooling negotiate from the strongest position.
